study: Landry et al. 2017, TEEM teacher PD x PALS parent program (2x2 factorial), Head Start pre-k (ECRQ)
eval_evidence: Conducted/authored by the Children's Learning Institute team that developed TEEM and PALS (IES R305A100212); the developers ran and reported the impact evaluation.
developer_evidence: TEEM PD (initial training, in-class coaching, coursework) delivered by project coaches supervised by senior research staff to ensure fidelity (p.683-696, 815).
cascade_evidence: Project coaches (research-team staff, supervised by senior research staff) deliver in-class coaching directly to teachers; no school lead-teacher train-the-trainer hop.
counterfactual_evidence: TPD contrast is the TEEM main effect; 'No TEEM' arm is explicitly 'control or business as usual' (n=38) (abstract p.43, p.653-654). PALS is a separate crossed parent factor, not a control alternative.
coaching_evidence: TEEM included individualized in-class coaching in fourteen 2-hr sessions approximately biweekly (~4 hr/month) plus side-by-side coaching and modeled lessons (p.693-696).
student_dose_evidence: TPD-vs-control contrast = TEEM main effect (teacher PD), which only changes the teacher's instruction; the PALS parent component is a separate crossed factor (parent-directed home program), not a direct student-facing instructional dose, and is collapsed across in the TEEM main effect.
maturity_evidence: Children measured pre-post across one Head Start pre-k year; school-readiness program implemented over a single academic year with no multi-year maturation axis.
